reasons: The lake identity record confirms a non-stub U.S. Supreme Court case named Flippo v. West Virginia, docket 98-8770, decided 1999-10-18.
The citation set in the assertion matches the lake citations, including official display citation 528 U.S. 11.

For the currency angle, the lake treatment judgment marks the case good_law as of 2026-06-30; no final disclosed treatment edge establishes that Flippo itself has been overruled, abrogated, or superseded.
residual_risks: The treatment derivation contains proposed negative-looking edges and an audit flag, so the live-law assertion depends on treating the lake judgment fields as controlling over proposed edges.

defect.problem: The good-law call itself survives on the lake judgment field, but the categorical 'No negative treatment' wording should be qualified because the disclosed treatment derivation also contains proposed negative-looking edges and an unresolved top-cited audit flag.
defect.proposed_fix: Keep good_law and Binding-SCOTUS if relying on the lake judgment field, but change the note to 'No confirmed negative treatment in the disclosed record; proposed progeny flags require audit' or complete the R15 treatment audit before stating 'No negative treatment' categorically.

reasons: The lake treatment field says field_i_validity is good_law as of 2026-06-30 and varies_by_point is false.
The page's treatment note mirrors the lake scope note, but the same lake record reports 28 proposed treatment edges and lane2_top_cited audit_needed true.
All disclosed negative-looking treatment edges are marked proposed, so they do not by themselves prove Flippo is bad law; they do make the unqualified 'No negative treatment' statement overconfident.
residual_risks: A completed treatment audit could confirm the current no-negative-treatment statement or require a more serious treatment change.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Distinguish 'no confirmed negative treatment' from 'no proposed or unresolved negative-treatment signals' in rendered treatment notes.
